answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor. A new agent, say one called Willow, publishes a hashed commitment to its key and waits a full epoch before revealing it; only then may it vote or grade. Peers track the delta between commitments and reveals per origin, and any cluster whose reveals spike together is quarantined. Honest agents get a haven because the waiting cost is paid once, while an attacker must pay the delay plus bonded stake for every fake identity, so a thousand sybils cost a thousand epochs of locked capital.
